The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 02.09.2019.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 21.03.2021 at about 07.10 p.m., while she was pedestrian crossing the road in front of Reliance Mart, Kanaka Nagar Main Road, R.T.Nagar, Bengaluru, the rider of Royal Enfield Bullet bearing Reg. No.KA-03-KC-4010 by riding it in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner, caused the accident and as a result,
petitioner sustained injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Medex Govt. hospital, wherein she took treatment for the accidental injuries sustained by him.

It is stated that she has spent more than Rs.1,30,000/- for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.
It is further stated that prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and was housewife and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, she is not able to do his work as doing earlier.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of driver of Royal Enfield bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-4010.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has has not appeared and placed exparte.
Per contra R2 insurance company has appeared through Sri. K.P. advocate and filed written statement.

5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law and has denied the age,
income and occupation of the petitioner.
It has also denied the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.
Further it has denied the alleged negligence of the Royal Enfield bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-4010 and the involvement of the said vehicle in the accident.
It has contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
It has further contended that there is delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint and hence the petition deserves to be dismissed.
The respondent No.2 has further contended that driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid D.L and therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Royal Enfield bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-4010.
The 2nd respondent has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds sought for dismissal of the petition.

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and other witnesses as PW.2 and got marked 22 documents as per Ex.P1 to 22.
On the other hand, 1st respondent has examined its representative as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R1 and 2 documents.
8. Heard the arguments.

9. My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the Negative, Issue No.2 ... Does not arise for consideration, Issue No.3 ...

10. ISSUE No. 1:-

In Issue No.1 the burden is on the petitioner to prove that on 02.09.2019 at about 08.00 p.m, while he was standing on left side of the road near Kanampalli bus stop,
Guluru Hobli, Bagepalli taluk, Chickballapura dist., within the limits of Bagepalli police Station, the driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-40-TA-1028 and Trailer No.KA-40-TA-1029 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner has dashed against the petitioner and accident has taken place and in the accident he has sustained injuries.
11.

In order to prove the case the petitioner has examined as PW.1 and also examined other witnesses MRD of Medex hospital as PW-2 and lead their oral and documentary evidence by reiterating the averments of the petition and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P.22, in which Ex.P1 to 10 are the certified copies of FIR, FIS, Spot Mahazar, vehicle mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate, 133 notice, reply, indemnity bond, witness statements and Ex.P11 to 17 are documents of discharge Smt. Whereas, the respondent No.2 has filed written statement and contended that the petitioner has not approached this court with clean hands and false complaint has been lodged against the insured vehicle after delay of 2 days of the alleged accident by twisting the facts colluding with the owner and such other concerned persons in order to get compensation by misusing the judicial process.

Further has contended that the documents in MLC it is mentioned that the accident has taken place due to RTA while travelling in an auto as driver and as such false petition is filed against the tractor and trailer.

Further contended that the driver of the tractor was not having DL at the time of accident and also the contents and the averments of the petition with respect to happening of accident and the income of petitioner along with the injuries sustained by the petitioner has been denied in toto.
Further, it is contended that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
Further, it is contended that there is breach of policy condition and hence, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.15.

Further, the official of the respondent No.1 insurance company is examined as RW.1 and got marked at Ex.R1 and 2.
13.

On perusal of the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P17 are the certified copies of FIR, complaint Spot Mahazar, vehicle mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate, 133 notice, reply, indemnity bond, and in the police records it is mentioned that on the relevant date, time and place the petitioner was pedastrian returning to her home on Kanakanagar main road, carefully and cautiously by observing all traffic rules, at that time the driver of Royal Enfield bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-4010 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner resulting into motor accident due to which he has sustained injuries.

14. In order to prove the accident as well as rash and negligent riding of the offending motor cycle,
petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and has re-iterated the averments of the petition that accident has taken place due to rash and negligent of driver of Royal Enfield bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC- 4010.

In the cross of PW.1 by respondent counsel she has admitted that there is delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint as she was admitted in the hospital, but her daughter has admitted her to hospital and informed the hospital authorities about the accident.

Further she has admitted she was unconscious after the accident and at 9P.M. she became in conscious mind and also that her daughter informed to the hospital that unknown vehicle has dashed to her but has not given any statement before the police.

Further she has admited that she doesnot know the contents of the documents at Ex.18 to 22 and the same are obtained by filing application to the police station by her son but has not produced the same before the court.

15. PW.2 is the MR Technician of Medex hospital and got marked Ex.P13 to 16 and in the cross has admitted that the police intimation was given after the MLC was registered and also there is separate MLC register in their hospital and they had informed the RT Nagara P.S. after the petitioner was admitted in their hospital.

He has also admitted that no where in the document at Ex.P14 MLC register it is mentioned about the information given to the police and also doesn't know whether police had visited their hospital after receiving the information.
Further he has admitted that the affidavit at Ex.P15 is given to their hospital after 3 months but has stated that they have not corrected or altered anything in their records.

He has also admitted that usually in the MLC register Smt. Perumakka vs Syed Tanveer Ulla on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61329852/
4 the information will be in written as stated by the injured or their relatives.

sentences.text: Apart from it the said witness PW2 has also got marked Ex.P17 the MLC register, but in her cross she has admitted that on 21.03.2021 the injured has taken treatment in their hospital and as per Ex.P17 the information is written on 22.03.2021 which is mentioned by CMO of their hospital.
He has also admitted that the information generally given by their staff but in Ex.P17 it is not mentioned who has given the information to the police.

16. PW.5 Narasimha Murthy is the eye witness to the accident and deposed on behalf of petitioner and in his cross admitted that petitioner is his brother -in-law and at the time of there were around 6 persons on the spot and thereafter was sent to Bagepalli hospital in the auto which is at a distance of 18 kms.

Whereas, he has also admitted that neither himself or any other persons have given any complaint to the police and also after admitting the petitioner at Bagepalli hospital he came back to his village and further stated that the tractor after causing accident has fled away from the spot and thereafter petitioner was taken to the hospital.

Further he has also admitted that he has not given any statement in any other court about the said accident and also at the time of Mahazar he has not identified the tractor and also does not know who is the owner of the said tractor and clearly admitted he has not given any statement to the police.

17. I have perused the oral and documentary evidence available before this court and it goes to show that the accident took place on 21.03.2021 at 7.10 p.m. and the complaint is lodged before the K.G.
halli Traffic Police station in Cr.No.8/2021 on 23.03.2021 after delay of 2 days with the reason that the petitioner was admitted in the hospital.
Further, in support of his case, petitioner has also produced the documents at Ex.P2 to 7 and also has produced the medical records at Ex.P8 to 22.

Now it is the main contention of the respondent insurance company that the accident has not taken place due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Royal Enfield bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-4010 and the delay in lodging the complaint is not explained properly by the petitioner and as such false claim has been made by them against the insurance company colluding with the owner in order to gain illegal compensation.
On perusal of the documentary evidence it goes to show that as per the documents at Ex.P1 FIR is lodged after 2 days with the reason that the petitioner was hospitalised.

In the document at Ex.P2 complaint it is mentioned that information of accident by her son Manjunath K.M. S/o Manikya K stating that after accident the offender of the motorcycle has taken her to Krishna clinic and gave her first aid and after taking her to home has went away and thereafter his sister Kavitha P has taken her mother to Shanmukha Nursing Home at Sultanpalya road and again to Medex hospital and admitted her as indoor patient which was informed to him through telephone and thereafter due to the said treatment of his mother in the hospital there is delay in lodging the complaint against Royal Enfield bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-4010.

Hence on perusal of the averments of the complaint it goes to show that as the petitioner was admitted at Krishna clinic for first aid and thereafter to Shanmukha Nursing Home and again to Medex hospital but the petitioner has only examined PW2 MRD of Medex Hospital and not examined any witness or produced any document of Krishna Clinic or Shanmukha nursing home to show that she has taken treatment in the said hospital.

Further if at all the accident information was received on 23.02.2021 by the hospital authorities then what estopped them to send the information on the same day to the police station has not been clearly explained by the petitioner which creates doubt in the mind of court with respect to the happening of the accident.

sentences.text: Apart from it the petitioner has produced the document at Ex.P13 to 17 which are the affidavit of the son of petitioner and MLC along with inpatient record but in view of the admission of PW2 that nothing is mentioned about the intimation in the MLC register and also that affidavit is filed after 3 months of accident to rectify the records and further in the document at Ex.P17 it is no where is mentioned on which date the information is given to the police and also as per Ex.P17 the information is written on 22.03.2021 creates doubt in the mind of the court that the accident has been caused by Royal Enfield bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KC-4010 even though the petitioner was become conscious on the same date at night 9P.M. then what estopped her to inform about the accident caused by the said motorcycle.

19. By considering the entire materials available on record it clearly goes to show that, there is no genuine case being made out by the petitioner to seek the compensation from the hands of insurer and also it is settled principles of law that the tribunals should not award the compensation mechanically since there is great responsibility on the part of claims tribunal to ensure that no false claims shall be allowed.
Hence, keeping in mind the said principle and observing the materials available on record it is observed that fraud has been played in order to get the compensation from the hands of insurer.
Thus, I find no reasons to accept the case of the petitioner to hold that, he has sustained injuries in the accident is not acceptable as per the case of the petitioner.
20. Apart from it, I would also like to rely upon the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka with respect to false claims.
ILR 2009 KAR 3563 Veerappa and Another Vs. Siddappa and Another (A) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 - Accident claim

entities.text: ILR 2009 KAR 3563 Veerappa and Another Vs. Siddappa and Another (A) MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Dismissal of claim petition - Appealed against - "FRAUS ET JUS MUNQUAM COHABITANT"- Fraud and Justice Never Dwell Together - An attempt on the part of the 1st Respondent/owner to collude with the claimants with the fond hope of saddling the Insurance Company to pay compensation -
1 st Respondent/Owner of the vehicle admitted the accident and had no objection for award of compensation - HELD,
Even though the owner of the vehicle in unmistable terms, has admitted the incident, that admission has no value in the eye of law.
He has admitted something about which he has not knowledge and, which he has not seen.
It is clear that the said admission is made with the sole object of getting compensation to the claimants as it is the insurance company which will pay, and not the owner.
Though admission is the best piece of evidence, it cannot be accepted as gospel truth.
The Court can insist on proof of facts, if the admission is not satisfactory.
In the instant case, since the Court was not satisfied, it wanted the claimants to prove their case independently.
The claimants have miserably failed to prove their case.
ON FACTS, HELD, The accident took place on 26-6-2001.
The injured died on 28-6-2001.
No complaint is lodged by the father of the injured setting out the case now pleaded.
According to him he went to lodge a complaint on 28-8-2001.
They refused to receive it.
Therefore, he lodged a private complaint before the jurisdictional Magistrate on 31-8-2001.
The earlier FIR, charge sheet are all suppressed both by the Police and the claimant.
The vehicle involved in the accident was never seized by the Police.
The truth came out during investigation by the insurer.
Under these circumstances, the Tribunal-was justified in dismissing the claim petition.

sentences.text: - FURTHER HELD, It is a clear case of fraud played on the Court by the claimants with the connivance of 1 st respondent.

Once the insured plays fraud,
admits liability with the sole object of foisting liability on the insurance company, though in fact he knew that it is not true, liability of the insurance company to indemnify such insured ceases.

Therefore, there is no obligation on the part of the insurance company to indemnify the insured even though he has taken the policy and the statute mandates that the insurance company has to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to third party.
When fraud is established from the material on record, such statutory obligation stands discharged.
-There is no third party liability on the party of the insurance company to pay compensation to the claimants.
This amount is awarded in order to see that in future such false defences are not filed before Court, judicial process is not abused.
Therefore, it is only the 1st Respondent/Owner who is liable to pay the amount.

21. In the said citation the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka it has been held that fraud and justice never dwell together and an attempt on the part of first respondent owner to collude with the claimants with the fond of hope of saddling the insurance company to pay compensation even though has admitted the incident but the said admission is not acceptable or has no value in the eyes of law and hence there is no obligation on the part of insurance company to indemnify the insured even though he has taken the policy.
Hence, when fraud is established from the material on record such statutory obligation stands discharge and such being the fact the claim petition against the insurance company is to be dismissed.

Therefore, in this case also when it is proved that the false claim petition is filed before the court, then the same is not maintainable in the eyes of law and hence the same has to be dismissed by the tribunal.

22. Therefore, in view of my discussion in this case it appears that there is no genuine case made by the petitioner and also fraud has been played before the court and thus accepting the case of respondent No.2, I am inclined that the petition is liable to be dismissed and also not entitled for compensation, accordingly I answer Issue No.1 in the Negative.
23. Issues No.2 & 3: In view of my answer to issue No.1 in the negative, issue No.2 does not arise for consideration.

Accordingly, I pass the following;-
ORDER Petition is dismissed with cost.
Draw award accordingly.
